Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: production pixel-art full-body sprite sheet for a side-view browser action platformer.
Input image 1 is ONLY the established character identity and pixel-art style reference, NOT the old short weapon or old repeated poses.
Subject: exactly the same scruffy young adult man, swept dark hair, black rectangular glasses, short beard, black sweatshirt, black trousers, dark sneakers. Preserve proportions, face and clothes. Same gritty limited-palette pixel art, crisp square pixels, no smoothing.
Weapon redesign: a LONG steel plumbing pipe with a small elbow at its tip, held in both hands. The straight pipe from grip to end is about 85% of the man's standing height, visibly much longer than in the reference. Consistent length and thickness in every pose; pale silver edge, dark steel interior. No hammer, sword, wrench, club head, or magic.
Composition: 1536x1024 landscape sheet, exactly FOUR columns and THREE rows, 12 separate complete full-body poses in reading order. Each cell has generous empty padding, every foot and pipe tip fully inside its cell, absolutely no overlap between sprites. Fixed camera facing screen RIGHT in all cells, no camera rotation. All feet on a common baseline within each row. Keep the man's standing anatomical scale constant even when crouching. Shift body weight by changing anatomy, not scaling. Flat uniform pure magenta #ff00ff background for the project's chroma-key importer. No shadows on background, no ground, no lines between cells, NO text, no labels, no effects, no motion blur, no trails, no extra objects.
Animation purpose: anticipation must be readable by silhouette alone. Separate weapon from hair and shoulders with visible background gaps; rotate torso and bend knees. The four active poses form ONE continuous forward stroke with the weapon tip reaching far to the RIGHT throughout the strike, not disappearing back beside the body. Hands and feet remain anatomically coherent. Full-body redrawing, not rotating a standing cutout.
Stroke 1: a committed forward diagonal cut, high-right to low-right, NOT a poke.
ROW 1 = anticipation, cells 0-3: (0) ready, knees flex and both hands start pulling behind right shoulder; (1) shoulders visibly twist away, hands lift behind head, pipe points diagonally up-left and is fully separated from head; (2) deepest loaded pose, weight over back foot, long pipe diagonal up-left, broad clear silhouette; (3) same strongest silhouette poised to release, head keeps looking right, elbows open. These must NOT be four copies of idle.
ROW 2 = active stroke, cells 4-7: (4) torso unwinds, both arms push forward/up, long pipe points diagonally up-right around -35 degrees; (5) arms extended forwards, pipe almost horizontal pointing right at lower chest height, maximum reach; (6) the same extended swing continues down-right at about +12 degrees, pipe tip still far to the right; (7) low forward follow-through with pipe about +25 degrees down-right, tip at shin height, knees absorb weight. Maintain arm extension and far forward tip reach, do NOT suddenly retract the pipe during active poses.
ROW 3 = recovery, cells 8-11: (8) hold the low fully extended endpoint; (9) elbows bend to draw the pipe back from low-right without a reverse attacking swing; (10) relaxed guard, weight centered; (11) ready guard matching the initial stance.
